_: TWO VOCABULARIES, DELIBERATELY SEPARATE. A BLOCK says what something IS. A SLOT says what kind of thing may live THERE. Collapsing them is how a graph came to own a size: the block was asked how big it should be, when the answer belongs to the slot the pattern gave it.
theOneRule: PAGE PATTERN OWNS THE SLOT · SLOT OWNS THE AVAILABLE GEOMETRY · MEDIA FAITHFULLY OCCUPIES THE SLOT.

slotTypes.reading: continuous prose the learner reads. Bound by the reading measure, always.
slotTypes.worked: a worked solution — ordered steps with their mathematics.
slotTypes.media: a figure, image or diagram. The slot gives a width; the media renders faithfully inside it.
slotTypes.workspace: a surface the learner acts ON — a writing pad, grid paper.
slotTypes.data: a table given a track of its own. A table inside an explanation stays in the reading slot; this type is for a page whose data IS the content.
slotTypes.examples: a collection of sibling worked examples, shown together or behind tabs.
slotTypes.questions: a question set. The one slot type that may own a local vertical scroll.
slotTypes.support: a key rule, definition or aside. Subordinate to a reading slot, never a substitute for one.

blockTypes.workedExample: a question, its worked solution and its answer
blockTypes.graph: a Cartesian plane with an authored domain
blockTypes.keyIdea: a rule or definition stated once, set apart

blockFitsSlot._: The build refuses a block placed in a slot this table does not permit. It is the compatibility check that replaces asking a block how large it wants to be.

occupancy.required: the pattern is not itself without this slot
occupancy.optional-collapse: absent → the slot disappears and the pattern uses its approved no-X subdesign
occupancy.optional-reserved: the emptiness IS part of the composition. Should be RARE, and every use is justified in the pattern record.
occupancy._: What must never recur: 'there are 400px left over beside the graph because the maths worked out that way'. That is not whitespace, it is layout residue.

mediaInASlot.rule: A GRAPH NO LONGER OWNS A SIZE. It receives a media slot and answers only: inside this width, at equal unit scale, this is the faithful rendering I can provide. Its height follows from the authored domain and the page grows.
mediaInASlot.whenItCannot: If the media's ASPECT CLASS means it cannot work in one subdesign, the pattern declares an approved alternative — chosen from the surface and the aspect class alone. It never negotiates width with neighbouring prose.
mediaInASlot.supersedes: `mediaSize` (compact | standard | large | workspace) was a useful FAILED intermediate: it proved that semantic importance and media geometry are separate concerns, which is why this layer exists. It is not the permanent mechanism — the slot is.

collection.tabs.appropriateWhen: the items are equivalent (three worked examples), the learner does not need to see them simultaneously, and quick switching is valuable
neverFor: items that must be compared with each other

views.tabs.means: ONE object seen in multiple REPRESENTATIONS
views.tabs.appropriateWhen: algebra | graph — the same fact, examined two ways
neverFor: items that must be compared with each other

details.means: an aside the learner may open

scroll.x.means: indivisible material overflows inside its own region
scroll.x.carriedBy: THE TABLE BLOCK, not a slot type. A table of values belongs to the explanation it is part of, so it appears inside a `reading` or `worked` slot far more often than in a `data` one — and the contract has to travel with the material, not with the track it happens to be in. The grammar previously said only a `data` SLOT could scroll sideways while the implementation attached it to the block; one of the two was wrong and it was the sentence.

expand.means: one object opened to the full surface

disclosure._: TABS ARE A DISCLOSURE PATTERN, NOT A SPACE-SAVING HACK. A layout may never reach for a tab because something did not fit, and the renderer may never create or remove one. Keyboard behaviour follows the W3C APG tabs pattern.
disclosure._evidence: GOV.UK tabs guidance (clearly labelled related sections, no need to see all at once, never for sequential or comparative content) and Mayer's segmenting principle (learner-paced segments beat one continuous presentation for complex material).

page.means: the document may get arbitrarily tall
page.rule: Virtually every teaching page. Never compressed to fit a viewport.

pane.means: an explicit TEMPLATE FEATURE — one pane moves while another stays
pane.rule: Never a renderer trick for making teaching content shorter. Teaching prose never sits in one.

spatialContiguity.rule: A BLOCK THAT EXPLAINS A VISUAL BELONGS TO THE SAME PATTERN AS THAT VISUAL — beside it, or immediately beneath it.
spatialContiguity._evidence: Mayer's spatial-contiguity principle: learners do better when corresponding words and pictures are near each other, because the search for the relationship is itself extraneous load.
spatialContiguity.consequence: It is a pattern-design rule, not a runtime one. Nothing measures anything to satisfy it.

pairingRule._: WHEN TWO SLOTS MAY SHARE A ROW. Derived from two side-by-side subdesigns that were designed, rendered, measured and removed — `visual.side` (a plane beside its reading) and `worked.single`'s `beside` (a scenario beside its solution).
pairingRule.rule: A row may pair two slots only when they are THE SAME KIND, deliberately given identical width — a comparison, where unequal heights read as 'one case was shorter' — or when AT LEAST ONE SLOT HAS A DESIGNED HEIGHT: a plotting pad, an instrument, a card.
pairingRule.forbidden: Two UNBOUNDED materials in one row. Such a row is sound only for the lengths the author happened to write, and how much prose an author wrote is content — which may never decide a composition. Both removals were exactly this.
pairingRule.pairsInTheCatalogue: caseA | caseB (same kind, identical width) · questions | workspace (the paper has a designed height) · instrument | prompts (the instrument does) · intro | support (a card). Nothing else pairs.
pairingRule.consequence: Every visual pattern stacks its media and its reading, and every worked example stacks its scenario and its solution. A taller page is the deliberate outcome.
pairingRule.reconciledWithSlotFit: SIDE-6 AND SIDE-7 PUT MEDIA BESIDE PROSE AGAIN, and the rule above had removed exactly that. They are not an exception to it — the rule's second clause now covers them, because what a media slot IS changed. `forbidden` names two UNBOUNDED materials in one row: material whose height depends on how much someone happened to write. Under the slot-fit contract a media slot is no longer one of those. Its width is the slot's, and its height is a deterministic function of that width and the authored domain — invariant to content, which the adversarial control proves on every render. A DERIVED height is a designed height. What the rule still forbids is prose beside prose, and that is still not in the catalogue. WHAT REMAINS TRUE FROM THE REMOVAL: a plane much TALLER than the prose beside it leaves a hole under the prose. That is why side-6 is approved for the `balanced` class only and side-7 for `landscape` only; a `portrait` plane has no side-by-side subdesign at any surface, and the column-residue control measures the hole rather than trusting the class.

rejected.bento: Automatic 'find aesthetically balanced cells for six blocks' placement. Attractive for dashboards and galleries; wrong for instruction, which has a pedagogical reading order. A grid is our alignment infrastructure, never an auto-placement algorithm.

mediaFit._: WHAT IT MEANS FOR MEDIA TO INHABIT A SLOT WELL. The catalogue solved 'what pattern is this?'. It did not solve this, and the visible result was a 760px graph left-aligned on a 1152px page with 392px beside it that had no role. Every media slot now declares a FIT and an ALIGNMENT.

fill.means: THE MEDIA MUST CONSUME THE SLOT WIDTH.
fill.forAGraph: slot width -> graph width; the authored domain and the equal-unit rule -> graph height. NEVER graph width -> a height cap -> a squeezed width. There is no height cap.
blocks: image (a major diagram or large instructional image)
fill.align: stretch — there is nothing to align, because the media is the slot's width
fill.check: painted media width == slot width, within 1.5px. Categorical.

contain.means: The media MAY be smaller than the slot, but must be DELIBERATELY POSITIONED.
blocks: image (a portrait photo, a small diagram, an illustrative or supporting figure)
contain.align: centre. START ALIGNMENT REQUIRES AN EXPLICIT DESIGN REASON, declared on the slot; without one, a contained object against the left edge is the defect this contract exists to name.
contain.maximum: the slot width. A contained object never exceeds it.
contain.check: painted media <= slot width AND centred within it, within 1.5px. Categorical.
contain.smell: If a contained object continually occupies only half its slot, that is evidence THE PATTERN SHOULD USE A SMALLER SPAN — not that the object should grow. The atlas reports it; a human rules.

theGraphRules: 1 · Graphs default to fit:fill, never intrinsic left alignment.
2 · A graph's width is the selected slot's width.
3 · Height is derived from graph geometry; normal lesson pages scroll. There is no height ceiling.
4 · A graph may use only the approved spans of its pattern.
5 · If an approved span is below the graph's minimum legible width, promote to the next approved span.
6 · If no span works, use the pattern's full-width state or its focus workspace.
7 · A contained graph must be centred; start alignment requires an explicit design reason.
8 · The build FAILS if a media slot contains anonymous horizontal residue.

whatTheMediaMayReport._: CAPABILITY, NEVER FOOTPRINT. A graph may say what it NEEDS. It may never say what it would LIKE — 'I would like to be 488px wide' is how tiny media ended up on large pages.
mayReport: that it requires equal unit scale
mayNotReport: anything about the page it is on
whatTheMediaMayReport.minimumLegibleWidth: THE NARROWEST PAINTED WIDTH AT WHICH NO TWO OF THE TEXTS THE FIGURE PAINTS OVERLAP — measured by painting and looking, not modelled. Measured because the engine's behaviour had to be discovered: it NEVER collides tick labels (it drops them), it never shrinks type (11px at every width from 200 to 1152), and its labelled-tick count is not monotonic in width — so 'retains its full labelling' was tried as a definition and discarded after measuring it. The only thing that ever collides is the AUTHORED objects' own labels, which is exactly what legibility means here.
whatTheMediaMayReport.theFinding: EVERY FIGURE THIS ENGINE CAN DRAW CLEARS THE SMALLEST APPROVED DESKTOP SPAN (4 columns = 368px). Span promotion is therefore implemented, deterministic and correct — and INERT at desktop. It binds only on a phone at 2 or 3 columns (183px, 283px). Saying so matters: the defect the maintainer is pointing at is NOT a legibility problem the media could have reported. It is the pattern's choice of span and alignment, which is what `fit` and the approved-span tables fix.

promotion.rule: CHOOSE THE SMALLEST APPROVED SPAN THAT SATISFIES THE MEDIA'S HARD CAPABILITY REQUIREMENTS.
promotion.notTheRule: Choose the prettiest arrangement based on content measurements.
promotion.why: It is not inventing a layout. It is selecting from layouts already designed and already approved — and the only input is a number the media reported about itself.
promotion.determinism: The approved subdesigns for a (surface, aspect class) are ordered by media span ascending; the first whose span clears the minimum legible width is taken. Ties cannot occur because two subdesigns of one pattern may not share a span at one surface, and the build refuses a pattern where they do.
promotion.noFit: If no approved span clears it, the pattern's widest approved span is taken and the build REPORTS it rather than silently shrinking the plane.

whitespace._: THREE KINDS, AND THE SYSTEM COULD NOT TELL THEM APART. It called all three reading margin.

readingMargin.is: Free columns beside a PROSE slot, because prose is bound by the reading measure and the page is wider.
readingMargin.test: The slot's type is `reading`, `support`, `worked`, `examples` or `questions`, and its span is the largest its pattern approves for prose at this surface.

patternWhitespace.is: Space inside an explicitly bounded media stage — a portrait diagram centred in a `contain` slot.
patternWhitespace.test: The slot declares `fit: contain`, and the media is centred within it.

slotResidue.is: An 8-column media slot, a 4-column graph stuck against the left, and the remaining columns with no role. THE EXAMPLES WE HAVE BEEN UNHAPPY WITH ARE MOSTLY THIS.
slotResidue.test: A `fill` slot whose painted media is narrower than it; or a `contain` slot whose media is not centred and which declares no reason to be start-aligned. Either fails the build.
slotResidue.theHarderCase: An 8-column media slot on a 12-column page, filled edge to edge, with 392px beside it. There is no residue INSIDE the slot and the media fits perfectly — and the page still reads as a graph stranded to the left. That is not a fit failure; it is the PATTERN having approved a span that leaves unnamed columns beside media. Free columns beside PROSE are reading margin; free columns beside MEDIA are not, because media has no measure to be bound by. The fix is in the approved-span table — a media span that is either the full grid or a centred block — never a measurement at render time.

whitespace.height: A tall page is completely acceptable. Height is unconstrained and the page scrolls. If a 6-column slot makes a tall graph 950px high, that is the right outcome.
whitespace.overflow: Local horizontal scrolling is allowed ONLY for components whose contract permits it — authored indivisible material (a table) and the tab strip.
whitespace.forbidden: Changing composition because one paragraph happens to be shorter.

slotInspector._: THE ANSWER TO 'IS THE MEDIA ACTUALLY INHABITING ITS SLOT WELL?' — a different question from 'what pattern is this?', and until now only the second had one. It turns what we were judging from screenshots into a contract.
slotInspector.oneOwner: ONE function judges a media slot. The control that fails the build and the overlay you look at both read it, so the picture and the build can never say different things. The overlay computes no verdict of its own.
reports: MEDIA SLOT (columns, span, granted px, painted px)
PAINTED MEDIA (what kind, and its actual size)
ASPECT-SCALE (px per x-unit, px per y-unit, and whether they are equal)
VERDICT — or DIAGNOSIS and LEGAL ACTIONS on failure
slotInspector.drawn: Over the render it measured: the slot dashed, the painted media outlined, and any unclaimed width hatched where it actually is — blue where the slot declared it (a centred `contain`), red where nobody did. Written beside every render that has media, as `<name>-inspect.png`.
slotInspector.notAResolver: NOTHING IT COMPUTES REACHES LAYOUT. There is no threshold at which it changes a span and no 'if occupancy < 55%, stack' — that is what made the system lose the design. Every verdict is categorical: the media consumes the slot, or it is contained and deliberately placed, or the build fails. The one non-categorical thing it does is PRINT A SIGNAL — 'this contained object occupies 41% of its slot' — which a human rules on by changing the pattern.
slotInspector.whichSlots: Slot types that hold an object with a footprint: `media` and `interactive`. Prose is bound by the reading measure instead; a workspace is a surface the learner acts on, not an object placed in one.
catalogueTime: every media slot declares a fit
`contain` + start alignment requires a declared design reason
a declared `mediaSpan` equals the columns its areas actually give
`approvedMediaSpans` matches the spans the subdesigns actually approve
a row whose only named slot is media is CENTRED OR FULL — never inset against one edge
slotInspector.caughtOnItsFirstRun: Three arrangements in the catalogue were stranded media and nobody had noticed: `visual.compare/paired` (8 of 12, four unnamed to the right), `media.full/inset` (the same, and named after the defect), and the tablet forms of both. `practice.workbook/beside` declared a 7-column media span for a 5-column slot.
